quests.instruction: Mateo is a son at home, a brother to his little sister, and a goalkeeper on his soccer team. What do we call these different parts a person plays?
quests.hint: Each one describes how Mateo connects to other people or what he does with them.
quests.explanation: A role is the part a person plays in a family or group. One person can have several roles at once, just like Mateo.
quests.funFact: The word 'role' comes from French. It first meant the roll of paper that an actor's lines were written on.

quests.instruction: Which sentence best describes what a parent does for a child?
quests.correctAnswer: Looks after, protects, and guides them 🛡️
options: Looks after, protects, and guides them 🛡️
Plays and wins every game for them 🎮
Does all of their schoolwork for them 📚
quests.hint: Think about what a growing child needs from the grown-up who raises them.
quests.explanation: A parent's role is to look after a child's needs, keep them safe, and guide them as they learn. Good guidance helps children learn to do things themselves.
quests.funFact: A foal can stand within about an hour of being born, but human children need many years of care while they learn.

quests.instruction: Which word names a role in a family, not a person's own name?
quests.hint: A role can be shared by many people, but a name belongs to just one.
quests.explanation: A name tells you who someone is. A role such as sibling tells you how people are connected, and many different people can share the same role.
quests.funFact: In Hindi, 'didi' means older sister, and in Turkish it is 'abla'. In both languages children often use that role word instead of the sister's name.

quests.instruction: Naomi wakes up hot and tired. Her caregiver puts a cool cloth on her forehead and calls a doctor. Which part of a caregiver's role is this?
quests.hint: Think about what Naomi needs most when she feels unwell.
quests.explanation: Caregivers look after a child's health. They notice when something is wrong, help the child feel better, and get a doctor when it is needed.
quests.funFact: A normal body temperature is about 37 °C. A temperature of 38 °C or higher is usually called a fever.

quests.instruction: Pablo is learning to tie his shoes. Which action shows a caregiver guiding him?
quests.correctAnswer: Showing him how, then letting him try 👟
options: Showing him how, then letting him try 👟
Tying them for him every single day 🙈
Telling him to wear sandals forever 🩴
quests.hint: Guiding means helping someone learn to do it on their own.
quests.explanation: A caregiver who shows a skill and then steps back gives the child a chance to practice. Doing everything for a child means they never get to learn.
quests.funFact: Many children learn to tie their own shoelaces somewhere between ages five and seven.

quests.instruction: Before crossing a busy road, Ritu's caregiver says, 'Hold my hand.' Which part of a caregiver's role is that?
quests.hint: Think about what could go wrong on a busy road.
quests.explanation: Keeping children safe is a big part of caring for them. Holding hands near traffic protects a child until they are old enough to judge the cars.
quests.funFact: Many road safety guides advise children to hold a grown-up's hand near roads until they are old enough to judge traffic, often around age eight.

quests.instruction: Which of these is part of a child's role in a family?
quests.correctAnswer: Learning, playing, and helping a little 🌱
options: Paying for all of the family's groceries 🛒
Deciding where the whole family will live 🏠
Learning, playing, and helping a little 🌱
quests.hint: Think about what children do each day at their age.
quests.explanation: A child's role is to grow, learn, play, and help in ways that fit their age. Big decisions and paying for things belong to the grown-ups.
quests.funFact: The United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child says every child has the right to learn and the right to play.

quests.instruction: Wen and her little brother are building a block tower together. Which words describe what siblings can be to each other?
quests.hint: Think about what Wen and her brother are doing right now.
quests.explanation: Siblings can play, help, and learn with each other. They may argue sometimes, but that is a normal part of growing up together.
quests.funFact: Many researchers who study children say that playing with siblings helps them practice sharing, disagreeing, and making up.

quests.instruction: Greta is ten and her brother Joon is three. Joon wants to join her game. What is a kind way for Greta to include him?
quests.correctAnswer: Give him a small part he can do 🧩
options: Say he is too little to play 🚫
Give him a small part he can do 🧩
Let him play only if he hands over his snack 🍪
quests.hint: Think about a part of the game that a three-year-old can manage.
quests.explanation: Older children can include younger ones by adjusting the game so everyone can take part. Joon gets to join, and Greta's game still works.
quests.funFact: Teachers call this kind of support 'scaffolding': giving just enough help so a younger child can try something new.

quests.instruction: When Nikhil was a baby, his grandmother carried him everywhere. Now Nikhil carries her shopping bag. What does this show?
quests.correctAnswer: Roles can change as people grow 🌱
options: Roles can change as people grow 🌱
quests.hint: Compare how Nikhil and his grandmother help each other then and now.
quests.explanation: As people grow, what they can do changes. A child who was once carried can learn to help and care for others too.
quests.funFact: In many families, children help older relatives with things like reading small print or using a phone.

quests.instruction: Mrs. Lee has a grown-up son. When he has a baby daughter, Mrs. Lee gets a new role. What is it?
quests.hint: Think about how the new baby is connected to Mrs. Lee.
quests.explanation: Mrs. Lee was already a mother. When her son has a child, she also becomes that child's grandmother. People add new roles over time.
quests.funFact: People often become grandparents in their fifties or sixties, though it varies a lot.

quests.instruction: Maya is a daughter at home, a goalkeeper on her soccer team, and a friend at school. Which of these is a family role?
quests.hint: Look for the role that describes how she is connected to the people in her family.
quests.explanation: Family roles, like daughter or sibling, describe how people in a family are connected. Goalkeeper and friend are roles in other groups.
quests.funFact: Everyone plays many roles in different groups, from home to school to a sports team.

quests.instruction: Zainab and Theo have the same parents, and Zainab is two years older. What is Theo to Zainab?
quests.hint: Compare their ages, then think about Theo's place among the siblings.
quests.explanation: Siblings share parents. Zainab is two years older, so Theo is her younger brother. Twins would be born on the same day.
quests.funFact: In Korean, the word for 'older brother' changes depending on whether the speaker is a girl or a boy.

quests.instruction: A babysitter looks after Diego while his parents are out for the evening. Is the babysitter a family member?
quests.correctAnswer: Not always; some are not relatives 🧑
options: Not always; some are not relatives 🧑
Yes, every caregiver is a relative 👪
Only if they stay there all night 🌙
quests.hint: Does a person need to be related to you to look after you for a while?
quests.explanation: A caregiver is someone who looks after a child, and some caregivers are relatives while others are not. Babysitters, teachers, and childcare workers all care for children.
quests.funFact: Many families also ask close friends or neighbors to help look after children.

quests.instruction: Which pair of roles can belong to the same person at the same time?
options: Child and parent of the same person 🔄
Older and younger than the same sibling ⚖️
quests.hint: Try to picture one person holding both roles with the same other person.
quests.explanation: A girl can be a daughter to her parents and a sister to her sibling at once. But nobody can be both older and younger than the same person, or both parent and child to the same person.
quests.funFact: One person can hold five or six family roles at once, such as daughter, sister, granddaughter, and niece.

quests.instruction: Why might a caregiver make a rule like 'no running in the kitchen'?
quests.hint: Think about hot food and sharp tools in the kitchen.
quests.explanation: Family rules often protect people from getting hurt and help the home run smoothly. A kitchen has hot things and sharp tools, so rules there matter.
quests.funFact: Hot liquids are a common cause of burns in young children, so many families have kitchen safety rules.

quests.instruction: Amara's family always takes shoes off at the door. Which action follows that rule?
quests.correctAnswer: Taking her shoes off at the door 👟
options: Leaving muddy shoes on the sofa 🛋️
Taking her shoes off at the door 👟
quests.hint: Follow what the family has agreed to do.
quests.explanation: Following a family rule means doing what the family has agreed on, even when it is easy to forget. Shoes off keeps floors and sleeping areas clean.
quests.funFact: In many countries, including Japan, India, and Korea, people take their shoes off before going into a home.

quests.instruction: Which sentence about family roles is true?
quests.correctAnswer: Every person has a role, including children 🌟
options: Every person has a role, including children 🌟
Only the oldest person has a role 👴
Babies and children have no role at all 🙈
quests.hint: Think about whether anyone in a family has nothing at all to give.
quests.explanation: Grown-ups care for and guide others, children learn and help, and babies are cared for. Each role matters, and no person is more important than another.
quests.funFact: A baby's smiles and coos help adults feel close to them, which is one way babies help build family bonds.

quests.instruction: Yusuf's little sister is learning to ride a bike. He runs beside her, steadying the seat. What role is Yusuf playing?
quests.hint: He is keeping her steady, not competing with her.
quests.explanation: Siblings can be helpers and cheerleaders for each other. Yusuf is giving his sister support while she learns.
quests.funFact: Many children now learn to balance first on bikes with no pedals, and add pedals later.

quests.instruction: Kofi's family calendar says: Monday, Mom collects him from school. Tuesday, Grandpa. Wednesday, Aunt Nia. Thursday, Dad. Who collects Kofi on the day after Grandpa's day?
quests.hint: Find Grandpa's day first, then look at the next one.
quests.explanation: Grandpa's day is Tuesday and the day after is Wednesday, which is Aunt Nia's day. Many families share the care of children and use a calendar to keep track.
quests.funFact: Sharing child care among several family members is common in many parts of the world.

quests.instruction: Which of these is mostly a caregiver's job rather than a young child's?
options: Putting toys back in a box 🧸
quests.hint: Which task needs money and planning for the whole family?
quests.explanation: Caregivers handle big jobs like buying food and paying for the home. Children help in smaller ways that fit their age.
quests.funFact: Many families let children help plan meals by choosing a vegetable or a recipe for the week.

quests.instruction: Which of these people is usually NOT a member of your family?
quests.hint: Think about who you usually meet at school rather than at home.
quests.explanation: Teachers, doctors, and neighbors help children a lot, but they are usually not part of the family. Parents and siblings are family.
quests.funFact: Some children call close friends of the family 'aunty' or 'uncle' out of love, even though they are not relatives.

quests.instruction: Farid is sick. The doctor checks him, and his father makes soup and sits with him. How are their roles different?
options: Both do exactly the same thing 🟰
quests.hint: One person is trained to treat illness. The other knows Farid well and loves him.
quests.explanation: Doctors use special training to find out what is wrong and treat it. Family members comfort a child and care for them at home. Both help in different ways.
quests.funFact: The word 'doctor' comes from a Latin word meaning 'teacher'.

quests.instruction: Bela says that only mothers can comfort a crying child. Is she right?
quests.hint: Think about all the people who have comforted you.
quests.explanation: Many caring people can comfort a child: parents, grandparents, brothers and sisters, aunts, uncles, and other caregivers. Comforting is about care, not about who someone is.
quests.funFact: Studies show that babies can form close bonds with several caregivers, not just one.

quests.instruction: Grandma Nur lives with her son Imran and Imran's daughter Selin. How many generations live in this home?
quests.hint: Think how many rows a family tree would need for these three people.
quests.explanation: Nur is the grandparent, Imran is the parent, and Selin is the child. Each is a different generation, so there are three generations in one home.
quests.funFact: Homes with three generations are common in many parts of Asia, Africa, and Latin America.

quests.instruction: Tobias is a son to his mom, a brother to his sister, and a grandson to his grandpa. How many family roles does Tobias have?
quests.hint: Count each different way Tobias is connected to someone.
quests.explanation: Son, brother, and grandson are three different roles, each connecting Tobias to a different person. Roles add up as a family grows.
quests.funFact: Once you add friend, classmate, and teammate, one child can have more than six roles.

quests.instruction: Two siblings need help from their caregiver at the same time. One needs a snack and the other has a scraped knee that is bleeding. Who should the caregiver help first?
quests.hint: Think about which need cannot wait.
quests.explanation: Caregivers often decide whose need is most urgent. A bleeding scrape needs cleaning quickly, while a snack can wait a minute.
quests.funFact: Rinsing a scrape with clean water soon after it happens helps prevent infection.

quests.instruction: Wen's grandfather helps with her reading, her brother Min shares his crayons, and her mom signs a school form. Which sentence sorts them correctly?
quests.correctAnswer: Her grandfather and mom are caregivers; Min is her sibling 🖍️
options: Min and her mom are caregivers; her grandfather is her sibling 👩
Everyone in the story is a sibling 👪
Her grandfather and mom are caregivers; Min is her sibling 🖍️
quests.hint: Sort each person by how they are connected to Wen.
quests.explanation: A caregiver looks after a child, so Wen's grandfather and mom are caregivers. Min shares Wen's parents and is her brother, which makes him her sibling.
quests.funFact: 'Sibling' comes from the Old English word 'sibb', which meant a relative.

quests.instruction: Elias, 8, sees his baby brother reaching for a hot mug while his dad is in the next room. What is the best way for Elias to act as a big brother?
quests.correctAnswer: Move it away or call Dad right away ☕
options: Ignore it because babies are Dad's job 🙈
Let the baby try it to see what happens 😬
Move it away or call Dad right away ☕
quests.hint: Safety comes first. He can act or call a grown-up.
quests.explanation: Even children can help keep a baby safe. When something could hurt, move it away if it is safe to do so or call a grown-up fast.
quests.funFact: Hot drinks can burn a toddler's skin, which is why they are kept out of reach.

quests.instruction: Which statement shows the best understanding of family roles?
quests.correctAnswer: Roles show how people connect and help 🔗
options: Roles show how people connect and help 🔗
Roles show who is better than others 🏅
Roles never change after a child is born 🔒
quests.hint: Think back to babies, big sisters, caregivers, and grandparents.
quests.explanation: A role describes how a person is connected to others and what they do. Roles can change over time, and no role makes a person more important than another.
quests.funFact: Studies of families around the world find that who does what at home varies widely from household to household.
